humanities_role_explanation: Historical petitions supply the items, but the benchmark is a purpose-built disciplinary annotation task (rhetorical section identification: Salutatio, Petitio, Conclusio) with a separate human-vs-model difficulty comparison. Items measure the disciplinary competence of identifying classical rhetorical structure; the paper reports distinct metrics for span tagging and for difficulty estimation.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only transcribed 18th-century Swedish and English petitions, tagged with inline XML-style span tags.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Identifying rhetorical sections (Salutatio, Petitio, Conclusio) as span tagging in historical petitions (structure extraction / rhetorical structure analysis); models also self-estimate document difficulty (0-2) compared with human difficulty ratings (uncertainty/difficulty self-estimation).

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to a single task (rhetorical section tagging) on one document type (petitions) in two languages.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: GPT-4, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Mixtral 8x22B, Mistral 7B, LLaMA 3 70B and 8B.

quantitative_metrics.note: Token-level precision, recall, F1, mean normalised token edit distance, mean error of difficulty and Spearman's rho.

summary: The paper builds datasets of 100 Swedish and 100 English historical petitions annotated for three rhetorical sections plus a per-document difficulty score. It evaluates six LLMs with few-shot prompts of varying detail and prompt language, and compares model-assigned difficulty to human ratings.
key_findings: Most models reach F1 in the high 90s for Salutatio; Petitio and Conclusio are harder, especially for smaller models and Swedish data. Prompt complexity has no consistent effect, cross-lingual prompting gives mixed results, and models generally underestimate document difficulty (mostly negative mean error; Spearman rho from -0.45 to +0.27).
facets_explanation: Three annotators manually inserted start and end tags, each petition annotated by two, with disagreements resolved after each batch and general principles agreed. Annotators appear to be project historians/linguists (not explicitly credited as domain experts, but the Swedish transcriptions were made by a historian). Gold is one tagged span set per section, scored by token overlap. Disagreement is reported as inter-annotator agreement and resolved, i.e. treated as noise.
results_explanation: Best headline F1 is LLaMA 70B on English Salutatio, long 3-shot: 99.9 (Gemini achieves 100.0 on Swedish Salutatio). Human inter-annotator agreement is reported (e.g. Swedish Petitio kappa 0.48, English Petitio kappa 0.68), but it is not on the same metric as model F1, so human_gap_points is null. The paper states models 'generally found both Petitio and Conclusio more challenging to annotate in the Swedish Petitions' than English. Prompt-variation comparisons were judged inconsistent by the authors and are not counted as a format gap.

humanities_role.quote: we focus both manual annotation and model evaluation on the sections Salutatio, Petitio, and Conclusio

dataset_size.quote: we have created a dataset of 100 historical petitions in Swedish and 100 in English
We also make use of an additional 10 petitions as a development set

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: how well LLMs can annotate rhetorical sections of historical petitions using few-shot prompting

gold_source.quote: we manually inserted start and end tags for each section. Three annotators carried out the work, with each petition annotated by two of them.

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: The models are instructed to annotate texts using predefined rhetorical tags

answer_multiplicity.quote: we compute token-level precision, recall, and F1-score by collecting all tokens that occur inside predicted spans and comparing them to all tokens inside the corresponding gold spans

plurality_treatment.quote: after each round, the specific disagreements were resolved and general principles agreed upon to support consistency in later batches

reported_cultural_asymmetry.quote: compared to the English data, the models generally found both Petitio and Conclusio more challenging to annotate in the Swedish Petitions
